entries.clue: Shown to be a devil, started badly (12)

indicatorNotes.badly: something done badly is done wrong, so the letters of STARTED come out in the wrong order

annotation.surface: Someone who began a task poorly has proved themselves a little devil.
annotation.walkthrough: The indicator only reaches STARTED; DEMON goes in unchanged ahead of the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thing demonstrated has been made visible or proved, which is what shown means in a past sense.

entries.clue: Get rid of some biased umpires (4)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters of the following words are used

annotation.surface: A call to sack the umpires who favour one side.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words, from the last letter of 'biased' into 'umpires'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you dump rubbish, or a partner, when you discard them without ceremony.

entries.clue: Raiment designed for mosque tower (7)

indicatorNotes.designed: something designed is put together in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Clothing has been made specially for a mosque's tower.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raiment' (an old word for clothing) is exactly the seven letters needed, and 'designed' sounds like tailoring rather than rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A minaret is the tall slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

entries.clue: In arena, a fitting canteen service (inits) (5)

indicatorNotes.In: the answer sits inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A suitable catering service is running in a stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: The NAAFI (Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes) runs shops and canteens for the British armed forces; '(inits)' warns the answer is a set of initials.
annotation.definitionFit: The NAAFI is the organisation that provides canteens for British service personnel.

entries.clue: Set off twice, then fly! (6)

indicatorNotes.off: something off is not right, so SET is rearranged
indicatorNotes.twice: the rearranged piece is written down two times

blocks.note: anagram fodder, SET taken two times
anagram indicator, applied to each copy of SET

annotation.surface: An instruction to start two things and then take flight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as one phrase meaning depart, and 'fly' as another verb of leaving; in fact 'fly' is the insect.
annotation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

entries.clue: Unusual name, one for a flower (7)

indicatorNotes.Unusual: the letters are put in an unusual order

annotation.surface: Someone has picked an odd name for a flower.
annotation.walkthrough: 'one' is spelt out as a word here, not turned into I: all its letters go into the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

entries.clue: Upright inhabitant of the rectory (5)

indicatorNotes.inhabitant of: the answer lives inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A morally upright person lives in the vicar's house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upright' suggests a virtuous vicar, but here it means standing straight.
annotation.definitionFit: Erect means upright, standing straight up.

entries.clue: First cook ready to empty mixed dish (4-3)

indicatorNotes.cook: to cook the books is to rearrange them dishonestly, so the letters of FIRST are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to empty: READY with its inside removed leaves only its outer letters

blocks.note: READY emptied of EAD leaves R…Y

annotation.surface: A kitchen instruction: first, the cook should get ready to serve a mixed dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'cook' reads as a person or a verb about food, and 'mixed' looks like an anagram indicator; in fact 'cook' rearranges FIRST and 'mixed dish' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A stir-fry is a dish of mixed ingredients fried quickly while being stirred.

entries.clue: Human nature to consume divine food (5)

indicatorNotes.to consume: the outer words swallow the answer, which sits inside them

annotation.surface: It is human nature to eat food that seems heavenly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Human' tempts a solver to write MAN and look for NA elsewhere, but the answer runs straight through the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Manna was the food sent from heaven to the Israelites in the wilderness.

entries.clue: East to allow chaps in – small amount (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'to allow chaps in' is read literally: the word for allow lets the chaps inside it

annotation.surface: A small number of men are let in from the east.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a border notice about letting men in from the east; the dash hides where the definition starts.
annotation.definitionFit: An element of something, as in 'an element of truth', is a small amount of it.

entries.clue: Railway buff educates clay worker (12)

annotation.surface: A railway enthusiast teaches a potter.
annotation.walkthrough: A trainspotter is a British hobbyist who notes down the numbers of passing trains; the word also means anyone obsessed with trivial detail.
annotation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is a railway enthusiast who collects locomotive numbers.

entries.clue: Conclude there's no place for the damned (7)

blocks.note: the word NO, taken as written

annotation.surface: Someone decides there is no hell after all.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a theological verdict, but 'no' is simply its own two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The Inferno, as in Dante, is hell, the place where the damned are punished.

entries.clue: Tell Huguenot if you're imprisoned (6)

indicatorNotes.imprisoned: the answer is locked up inside the words before it

annotation.surface: A plea to inform a French Protestant if you are jailed.
annotation.walkthrough: The Huguenots were French Protestants persecuted in the 16th and 17th centuries, which is why imprisonment fits the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: you notify the authorities when you officially tell them something.

entries.clue: Wreckage of mast drifting around lake (7)

indicatorNotes.drifting: letters that drift move out of place
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around L

blocks.note: the letters of OF MAST rearranged

annotation.surface: The broken remains of a ship's mast float about on a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder; F(L)OTSAM.
annotation.definitionFit: Flotsam is the wreckage of a ship or its cargo found floating on the water.

entries.clue: Animal about to hug payee (6)

indicatorNotes.to hug: the bear wraps itself around RE

blocks.note: re = about, as in memo headers

annotation.surface: A bear is on the point of embracing someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is RE and 'to hug' is the instruction: BEA(RE)R. A cheque made out to 'bearer' is paid to whoever holds it.
annotation.definitionFit: The bearer of a cheque is the person who presents it and is paid.

entries.clue: Improves parts of tennis game (7)

blocks.note: the sense used of a patient or share price that recovers
a rally is an exchange of shots in tennis

annotation.surface: A tennis player's game gets better in places.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as one sentence about getting better at tennis.
annotation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover or improve; rallies are also the exchanges of shots that make up a tennis match.

entries.clue: New experiences of top degrees (6)

blocks.note: a first is something done for the first time
a first is the top class of British university degree

annotation.surface: Getting the best university results is a novel experience.
annotation.walkthrough: British university degrees are graded, and a first (first-class honours) is the highest grade.
annotation.definitionFit: Firsts are both things done for the first time and top-class degrees.

entries.clue: Conceal my oil spillage without waste (12)

indicatorNotes.spillage: spilled letters land in a new order

annotation.surface: Hide the oil I spilt, and don't waste any clearing it up.
annotation.walkthrough: An oil spill is the opposite of economy, which gives the surface its irony.
annotation.definitionFit: Economy in its older sense is careful management of resources, so acting in that spirit means wasting nothing.

entries.clue: Missing a brass band sound's great energy (5)

indicatorNotes.Missing: a word missing something lacks it, so the band sound is written without the A

blocks.note: oompah imitates a tuba's deep notes

annotation.surface: A brass band without an oompah loses all its energy.
annotation.walkthrough: OOMPAH minus A leaves OOMPH; the ''s' stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal word, probably imitative, for the vigour or punch that makes something exciting.

entries.clue: Church surface where change spoken of (5)

indicatorNotes.spoken of: the word is said, not written

annotation.surface: A church spot where people talk about changing things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'surface' is a stretched but fair word for the table on which communion is prepared.
annotation.definitionFit: The altar is the table, a flat surface, at the front of a church.

entries.clue: Change poor diet (4)

indicatorNotes.poor: a poor version is a badly put-together one

annotation.surface: Advice to fix an unhealthy diet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change' reads as the anagram signal, but it is the definition; 'poor' does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, narrowed: editors change texts and films, cutting and revising them.

entries.clue: Goddess finding Meissen potty! (7)

indicatorNotes.potty: potty is British slang for crazy, so the letters go crazy

annotation.surface: Someone discovers a goddess figurine on a piece of Meissen pottery.
annotation.walkthrough: Meissen is a famous German porcelain, so 'potty' looks like it means a pot; here it is slang for mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in Greek myth she punished human arrogance, which is why an arch-enemy is now called a nemesis.

entries.clue: Sampled first of roughage in new diet (5)

indicatorNotes.first of: take just the opening letter of 'roughage'
indicatorNotes.in: R goes inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.new: DIET made new comes out in a different order

annotation.surface: Someone has had a taste of fibre as part of a new eating plan.
annotation.walkthrough: R goes inside the rearranged DIET: T(R)IED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dish you tried is one you tasted, which is the food sense the surface supports.

entries.clue: Scientist bursts tyres with experimental toy (9,3)

indicatorNotes.bursts: a burst tyre is blown apart, so its letters are scattered

annotation.surface: A scientist blows out tyres with a toy used for experiments.
annotation.walkthrough: 'bursts' looks like a verb with the scientist as its subject; it is the instruction to rearrange TYRES.
annotation.definitionFit: A chemistry set is a children's kit for doing simple experiments.
